rule: fixed by seed number, declared BEFORE any P4 data was read: seeds 6-29 -> fit, seeds 30-35 -> holdout
rationale: data/eval/ (seeds 36-40) is locked until P10 as the Tier-C evidence; touching it at P5 spends it early and invalidates every reported number (CLAUDE.md rule 15).
P5 therefore needs its OWN held-out set for the out-of-sample validation scatter and R2 — that is what holdout_seeds provide.
Split is by seed, never by row (rows within one run are heavily correlated — CLAUDE.md rule 6/15).
The rule is a fixed function of the seed number (first 24 / last 6 of the training batch), chosen without looking at any per-seed statistic, so no selection effect can enter.

consumers.P5_fitting: GLM fits and model-comparison tables (AIC/BIC) use fit_seeds only
consumers.P5_validation: out-of-sample scatter, R2, raw-vs-clipped comparison are evaluated on holdout_seeds
consumers.P10: data/eval seeds 36-40 stay untouched by everything above

immutability: same mechanism as frozen/normalization.json: never overwrite; if it must change, create split-v2.json and record why in the phase report
